OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-84.51274,39.10128.name: Cincinnati Children's Research Foundation
-84.51274,39.10128.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.14480,51.52357.name: Lister Fertility Clinic at The Portland Hospital
-0.14480,51.52357.state: 1st Floor, 215 Great Portland Street, London, W1W 5PN
-0.14480,51.52357.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

114.05790,22.54310.name: He Jiankui — the germline case and its aftermath
114.05790,22.54310.desc: The Chinese scientist who produced the first gene-edited babies in 2018, was imprisoned, and has since resumed publicly promoting embryo editing. The case remains the only criminal enforcement of a germline prohibition anywhere, and the fact that he is working again is part of the record.

114.05790,22.54310.name: BGI Genomics — clinical and prenatal testing
114.05790,22.54310.desc: Prenatal screening at very large scale, and the operation behind Western government concern about where genetic data ends up. Prenatal testing generates genomic data on people who never consented to research use, which is a question every large provider faces and few answer publicly.

114.05790,22.54310.name: BGI — MGI Tech instruments
114.05790,22.54310.desc: BGI's instrument arm, which built sequencers to escape dependence on Illumina after patent litigation restricted its access in several markets. It is the only serious challenge to a near-monopoly on the machines that read DNA, and the dispute has been fought in courts on three continents — which makes the price of sequencing partly a function of patent law rather than of engineering.

72.57140,23.02250.name: Hester Biosciences
72.57140,23.02250.desc: An Indian animal health company holding around fifteen per cent of the national veterinary vaccine market, concentrated in poultry, and with manufacturing in Africa as well as India. Poultry is where recombinant vector vaccines are used at the largest scale anywhere — given in ovo, before the bird hatches — and the producers already on this map are all European or American. A company at this share of one of the world's biggest poultry sectors is a material part of who administers engineered viruses to animals, and its absence would leave that trade looking like a transatlantic one.
